pr.title: Make Calibrate backend targeting build-time only
pr.body:
## Summary

Calibrate currently exposes native backend selection and promotes self-hosting in Advanced settings. A build configured for a different backend could also inherit globally stored credentials unless startup first establishes their origin.

This change removes runtime backend controls and URL route inputs. Native/internal builds use `EXPO_PUBLIC_CALIBRATE_SERVER_URL`; production browsers use their serving origin. Native startup retains a session only for a known matching origin. A changed target requires fresh sign-in, while pending or unreadable local state blocks the transition and preserves the original data with recovery guidance.

Closes #438. This is the focused client successor to #439; its deferred administrator/bootstrap work and original evidence remain preserved. No parent PR, backend/auth-stack changes or release-helper changes are included.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

| Scenario | Expected and observed |
| --- | --- |
| Open Advanced settings | Hosting promotion and switching controls are absent; diagnostics and software updates remain. Matched browser captures below and maintained native component tests passed. |
| Start with matching, changed or unknown legacy origins | Matching sessions retain credentials. Safe changed targets start signed out; queued changes, unknown identity, unreadable storage and interrupted writes preserve originals and block unsafe authentication/replay. Maintained migration, storage and startup-gate regressions passed. |
| Complete old requests after logout/account replacement | Old callbacks cannot obtain replacement credentials or clear the replacement session. Late native tokens are queued for revocation; stale browser cookies are revoked before replacement login. Failed revocation blocks replacement until recovery. Maintained session-race tests passed. |
| Request password reset with a legacy backend URL parameter | The request remains on the serving origin. A synthetic 503 displays retry guidance without changing destinations; both independent browser captures and recorded request URLs confirm this. |

### Before / After

**Advanced settings:** removes self-hosting promotion while preserving support diagnostics and update controls.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Advanced settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/a7d2ad1648d2b743cdfda5ef66950f6feee741ad/managed-438/before-advanced.png) | ![After: Advanced settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/0ad646c474e5b95a4d6230419cb73528d0debcae/managed-438/review-final/after-final-advanced.png) |

**Password-reset failure:** recovery remains available on the serving origin. These are independent captures of intentionally unchanged UI.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: reset failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/a7d2ad1648d2b743cdfda5ef66950f6feee741ad/managed-438/before-recovery-failure.png) | ![After: reset failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/0ad646c474e5b95a4d6230419cb73528d0debcae/managed-438/review-final/after-final-recovery-failure.png) |

Before is actual master `4cbcbc740fbe5fa5646b4de31951c79a653176d5`; After is `8e109f51598ce12a2fd0d69503d3432713696f4c`. Current head `60eca5e0add3cf612041f8a5ad5400fbd33b7abe` changes only a test timeout; [capture applicability](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/296ef4f724d2c0e8c808ea6192a06a10c7a24b73/managed-438/checkpoint-60eca5e0/evidence-applicability.json) is unchanged. Separate builds used the same synthetic fixtures, 1280x1100 light browser viewport and frozen inputs. The shared harness hides unrelated transient PWA notices; compared UI pixels are unaltered. [Final provenance](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/0ad646c474e5b95a4d6230419cb73528d0debcae/managed-438/review-final/provenance.json), [fixture/hash clarification](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/a7d2ad1648d2b743cdfda5ef66950f6feee741ad/managed-438/provenance-notes.json), [artifact digests](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/0ad646c474e5b95a4d6230419cb73528d0debcae/managed-438/review-final/artifact-digests.json) and [complete scope](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/296ef4f724d2c0e8c808ea6192a06a10c7a24b73/managed-438/checkpoint-60eca5e0/scope.json) are retained outside product history.

## Supporting checks and limitations

Passed: mobile typecheck; 235 mobile suites/1,332 tests; 69 API-client tests; 251 release-configuration tests; four maintained desktop/compact PWA checks; independent Before/After web builds and four capture pairs; Android JavaScript export.

Native-device/emulator checks are deferred and unexecuted; component tests and bundling are not device execution. The [current-head Codex review](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/450#issuecomment-6066642825) found no major issues. Current-head CI is complete: 14 checks passed, 11 skipped, none failed. Android/iOS builds, web smoke/build, mobile tests, typechecks, release configuration and vulnerability scanning passed. Database upgrade/rollback checks were skipped; earlier retained records are historical and do not establish current-head execution. Independent QA remains pending. Actual GitHub page-rendering inspection is waived under the recorded human amendment; genuine captures and independent pixel inspection remain required.

commit.message:
Block release finalization until exact candidate CI succeeds (#434)

## Summary

Cut release could merge its generated PR before CI started: PR432 merged
while five workflows expired awaiting approval. This change waits for
successful CI on the exact release candidate, checks again immediately
before merge, and keeps a blocked candidate available for recovery.
Stage summaries distinguish validation, merge and publication from
optional OTA/deployment skips.

Refs #433. Independent of overlapping draft #401; that branch is
unchanged and its future integration must preserve this gate.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

This is a non-UI workflow change. [Source-bound evidence, commands and
complete
scope](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/825306680fb8430bd8cf02c4c5a99724c44773b5/final-contract.md)
compare master `6b803fbc` with this implementation `cf388c52`.

| Scenario | Intended and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| PR432-style approval expiry with zero jobs | Before, finalization
could merge without inspecting CI. The maintained synthetic regression
now rejects it; missing workflows and pending approval also fail closed
at a bounded deadline. |
| Five exact-candidate workflows succeed | Gate permits finalization
only with required successful jobs and documented release-only skips.
Wrong PR or tested base, missing/ambiguous run associations, refs moving
during inspection, failed jobs and newer failed attempts reject. |
| Approval arrives while waiting | Synthetic pending-to-success polling
passes; perpetual pending approval times out. No approval is automated.
|
| Failure guard deliberately disabled | The retained mutation experiment
detects the unsafe variant; the final maintained gate suite passes all
20 tests. |

## Supporting checks and limitations

- Maintained release suite: 152 passed; two existing Linux-only
publisher-shell cases skipped on Windows. YAML and four inline scripts
parse; diff hygiene passes.
- Preserves explicit publication dependency, immutable recovery and
current write scopes. Finalization uses Actions read access already
granted to its caller; no new privileged trigger or credentials.
- GitHub may still require human approval of bot-created PR workflows.
This change waits and reports that requirement. Approval-free automation
is a separate authorization decision.
- No live release dispatch, merge, publish or deployment was exercised.
Server-side required-check rules remain an administrator decision;
polling cannot make CI/base validation and merge atomic.

issue.title: Focus Calibrate on hosted use with build-time backend configuration
issue.body:
## Problem

People using Calibrate should get a focused hosted experience without choosing or setting up a backend. Current native sign-in and Advanced settings expose server selection, and PR439 expands that workflow. The [new human direction](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/issues/405#issuecomment-6049386828) supersedes those customer-facing hosting requirements. Internal/development builds still need a fixed backend chosen when the app is built.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Remove customer-facing backend pickers, service-switching settings, URL route inputs and self-hosting promotion. No hidden developer picker. Keep useful diagnostics, compatibility/retry behavior and authorized administration.
- Use the existing public build input, `EXPO_PUBLIC_CALIBRATE_SERVER_URL`, for native/internal targets; production browser requests stay on the serving origin. Validate explicit configuration and fail closed on invalid targets. Channel names alone must not select URLs. Do not choose a new production domain or hardcode private project/account values.
- Bind authentication, recovery and credentials to the configured origin. Preserve account/session-generation checks, logout/revocation and late-response isolation. A changed target clears active credential/consent state before new authentication, without reusing another server's tokens.
- Migrate legacy saved choices safely before authenticated requests or offline replay. Preserve origin/account-scoped health data, outbox, drafts and recovery state. Pending/failed/replaying or unknown local state blocks a target transition with clear recovery guidance; no automatic cross-server replay, reassignment or silent deletion.
- Preserve useful development/build tooling and backend authorization/data safeguards. Earlier unmerged administrator/bootstrap work remains retained for later consideration rather than being deleted or silently included in this narrower change.
- Validate fixed-target resolution, legacy and interrupted transitions, storage failures, session races and recovery destination with maintained regressions. Demonstrate representative actual-master-to-final browser changes with genuine matched captures and exact provenance. Native-device checks remain explicitly unexecuted/deferred for review readiness under the [human amendment](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/issues/405#issuecomment-6041659686).

No production data migration, backend-role removal, infrastructure cleanup, provisioning, credential changes, deployment or release is included. Unified release-pipeline work has separate ownership.

## Implementation plan

Propose a focused successor from reverified master: define the fixed-target/bootstrap migration contract, remove runtime selection and promotional copy, selectively retain PR439's relevant client isolation fixes and maintained tests, then validate the final published scope and behavior. Preserve PR439 and all original evidence; do not restructure or close it until the coordinator records the intended treatment of its deferred backend scope. Coordinate shared documentation/build configuration with the release owner; keep auth PR431/437/442 independent. The [source inventory and build-time findings](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/issues/438#issuecomment-6049586161) remain the implementation plan.

[Exact original requirements](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/5a0e855ae28d74ce70e365006821e19588ed8499/native-deferral-result-20261007/issue438-after.md) and [original recovery plan/history](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/6b265afbb92951ba55e1c22212374225049c580e/pr402-recovery/recovery-plan.md) remain retained.

## Implementing Codex task

Implementing owner: verified native task ID `01a11c7b-b7fa-7578-9694-80a1cae2b03d` (shareable URL unavailable). This explicitly replaces the completed prior owner; its history is retained in the [predecessor issue record](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/a7d2ad1648d2b743cdfda5ef66950f6feee741ad/managed-438/issue438-before.md).

## Implementing PR

Active implementing PR: [PR450](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/450) (draft, managed-first client scope). [PR439](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/439) remains open and unready with its deferred backend work and original evidence retained; closure requires coordinator verification. Historical original: [PR402](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/402), closed without merging; source/evidence remain retained.

## Problem

Native users need a deliberate service choice that keeps credentials and recovery on the intended server. Self-hosted operators currently rely on environment-based administrator grants and need durable user-role management, safe first-owner setup and recovery. PR402 contains unmerged improvements, including a directory scan that holds the ownership lock and can block other account operations.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Preserve managed hosting as the default. Make native self-hosted selection explicit, tested and cancelable; failed/canceled selection preserves the current destination. Confirming a different service clears entered credentials and consent. Browser authentication and recovery remain on the serving origin.
- Separate Service & hosting from app diagnostics. Explain account/service boundaries and prevent switching while offline changes are unresolved or their state is unknown.
- Provide a bounded administrator directory containing only account ID, email, role, creation time and verification status. Require explicit role-change confirmation, fresh verified-admin authorization and last-verified-admin protection for demotion and deletion. Directory reads must not hold the exclusive ownership lock.
- Atomically grant exactly one first-account owner only on a genuinely new self-hosted database; never on managed hosting or a populated upgrade. Import valid existing legacy administrator IDs once, preserve an unverified owner's account after email-delivery failure, and recover only an existing verified account. Never reserve grants for future users.
- Preserve immediate authorization and account/server isolation across logout, refresh, cancellation and late responses, including master's offline workspace and revocation behavior. Keep issue421's credential-verification and atomic native-login contracts intact.
- Validate the database invariants with real cross-connection PostgreSQL cases, fresh/populated upgrade and rollback checks, and maintained client/API regressions. Demonstrate representative actual-base-to-final behavior with matched synthetic captures, including the native chooser. Historical After-only web images are not baseline evidence.

No provider activation, production account/access changes, credential changes, deployment or release is included. This scope follows the trusted human authorization for PR402 recovery and active backlog progression; related closed issues290/298 are context, while421/422 remain separate outcomes.

## Implementation plan

Follow the [retained recovery plan](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/6b265afbb92951ba55e1c22212374225049c580e/pr402-recovery/recovery-plan.md) for a focused successor from reverified master: preserve original evidence, selectively port useful product/tests/contracts/documentation, fix directory locking, and resolve the seven identified auth/API-client/rollback conflicts. Coordinate shared imports and test loaders with the existing421 owner; do not import or rewrite PR431/437. Keep capture archives and one-off capture machinery outside the successor's published product history. The authorized continuation is implemented in draft PR439. CI and matched browser evidence are complete. Actual native chooser evidence remains blocked by unavailable device/emulator access; independent engineering review/QA is pending.

## Implementing Codex task

Implementing owner: verified native task ID `01a1145f-aae2-70e0-af56-3952f0eab012` (shareable URL unavailable). This follows the original cloud owner `/root/improve_self_hosting_experience` and its [explicit idle handoff](https://github.com/MChartier/agentic-development-workflow/blob/e7c61c50d8be01437c15e0c3cfcd3fa683e81571/runtime-next-scope/pr402-owner-handoff.json).

## Implementing PR

Active implementing PR: [PR439](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/439) (draft). Historical original: [PR402](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/402), retained open until the coordinator verifies replacement, evidence and dependencies.

Managed-first planning is complete; no product changes or tests were run. Recommendation: a focused successor from actual master. PR439 publishes one commit across 63 files (+3,360/-729), including backend roles, migration and administration. An in-place reversal would retain superseded chooser work and broaden the published review range. Preserve that branch, backend work, tests and evidence; this proposal does not authorize closure or history rewriting.

| Source/path inventory | Proposed treatment |
| --- | --- |
| `mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx`, `register.tsx`; `mobile/src/components/ServerUrlControl.tsx`; `auth/authServerDraft.ts` | Remove chooser, candidate state and backend URL route inputs. Keep credential validation, consent and submit guards. |
| `mobile/app/forgot-password.tsx`, `reset-password.tsx`, `verify-email.tsx` | Bind recovery to the configured native/serving browser origin; incoming route parameters must not select an endpoint. |
| `mobile/app/(tabs)/(settings)/advanced.tsx`, `settings.tsx`; `settings/SettingsHome.tsx`, `navigation/routeRegistry.ts` | Remove runtime connection setup and hosting promotion; retain diagnostics, software updates and authorized admin access. Do not port PR439's `service.tsx` route or hosting overview/promotion. |
| `README.md`, `mobile/README.md`, `mobile/app.json`, `legal/publicLegalContent.ts` | Remove promotional onboarding and OS-permission wording; use accurate development/internal-purpose wording where needed. Keep factual independent-operator privacy/deletion boundaries and internal deployment instructions. Actual `mobile/app/index.web.tsx` already has no self-hosting promotion. |
| `mobile/src/config/server.ts`, `auth/storage.ts`, both `AuthContext` files, `offline/{database,provider,queuedMutation}` | Make the build target authoritative; add origin-bound startup migration before credentials/replay. Retain PR439's session-generation isolation fixes selectively. |
| `auth/offlineWorkspace.ts`, `auth/logoutIntent*`, `onboarding/draftStorage.ts`, `healthConnect/storageScope.ts`, `wear/*` | Preserve origin/account namespaces, pending revocation and retained health data. Verify consumers never inherit a new target's credentials. |

Migration contract: equal known legacy/configured origins retain their session. A different known target requires fresh authentication and cleared active credential/consent state; never relabel old tokens or data. Unknown/malformed legacy identity, unreadable storage or any pending/failed/replaying changes holds startup before authenticated network/replay and preserves the originals. Provide retry and matching-build recovery guidance, without a runtime selector or automatic discard. Make migration restart-safe and inspect all relevant old namespaces, not only the currently visible account. With a proven empty outbox, preserve old local records while starting a separate target session.

Reusable release-owner facts:

- `EXPO_PUBLIC_CALIBRATE_SERVER_URL` is read directly by `config/server.ts`. Native defaults are configured URL, otherwise existing hosted production or simulator loopback in development. Today a persisted native choice overrides release defaults; development configuration overrides the saved choice. Tokens are currently global SecureStore keys. Browser production ignores native saved/configured choices and uses its serving origin.
- `mobile/eas.json`: internal channel uses preview environment; production uses production; iOS simulator extends internal. `app.config.js` independently reads `EXPO_UPDATES_CHANNEL` (default internal) and `EXPO_PUBLIC_EAS_PROJECT_ID`, uses appVersion runtime policy, and sets update request headers. Channel is update routing, not the backend URL. EAS profile channel and the custom header input must agree.
- `scripts/expo-native-dev.mjs` already supplies the explicit URL from process/repository build environment or allocated simulator port. `native-release-build.mjs` validates a credential-free HTTPS origin and supplies it to phone and Wear. `native-internal-release.mjs` currently overwrites URL/project/channel with fixed instance constants; generalizing that release helper belongs to the release owner, without new hardcoded private values.
- Local `native-ota-contract.mjs` records endpoint/project/channel/runtime; `native-ota-update.mjs` rejects mismatched environment or channel. CI `expo-ota-artifact.mjs` validates and binds the environment to source/channel/project, but its URL validator is less strict about origin-only paths. Carry one explicit normalized endpoint through build/export/OTA receipts; do not assume channel or appVersion protects endpoint identity. Endpoint values embedded in a shipped app are public configuration. See [Expo environment semantics](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/environment-variables/) and [channel/runtime semantics](https://docs.expo.dev/eas-update/how-it-works/).

Dependencies: proposed client work needs no parent from backend stack431 ->437 ->442 and must preserve its HTTP/session contracts. Deferring PR439's backend portion avoids their overlapping auth routes/loaders. PR441 and the separate unified-release intake overlap README/mobile documentation and `native-internal-release.mjs`; coordinate those boundaries, with pipeline/versioning/server/native/OTA/iOS publication owned separately.

Validation after implementation: target-resolution and two-origin migration matrix (same/different/missing/malformed, interrupted writes, unknown storage, offline queues and rollback to a matching build); stale request/refresh/logout and recovery tests; customer UI/route absence; relevant mobile/API/type checks and configured CI. Use actual master as Before, fresh final browser captures plus source/build/fixture provenance, independent pixel review and complete ordered commit/file assessment. Native device execution stays deferred and explicitly unperformed. No user decision is currently required for this bounded plan; coordinator branch admission is the next operational step.

Implementation admission claimed for the focused managed-first successor described in the existing plan. The prior owner is verified completed/idle; its PR439 branch, deferred backend work and evidence will remain preserved. Desktop reinstallation changed the connection, so the new task will record an explicit ownership handoff rather than claim conversation migration. Actual master is unchanged at 4cbcbc74. Root coordination will verify task execution before recording a new owner; this claim is not started implementation. Independent QA and full evidence gates remain.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Invalidate stale browser authentication responses**

When an earlier browser login or registration finishes after a later authentication action, the browser has already applied that stale response's session cookie before this epoch check returns `false`. The UI can therefore retain the replacement user while subsequent credentialed requests use the earlier account, or a login completing after logout can silently restore a session on reload. Stale browser auth responses need a server-side invalidation/serialization path rather than only ignoring their payload.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L13-L16](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/8a6d1af405a8fbabfc9fdd9d2120eef510f5bd36/AGENTS.md#L13-L16)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Allow empty existing installations through migration**

An existing installation that was merely opened but never signed in already has a device ID because startup always calls `getOrCreateDeviceId`, but it has no persisted server URL, credentials, or server-scoped state. This check throws before `inspectLocalState()` can establish that the installation is empty, so upgrading such an installation permanently stops at the recovery screen even though there is nothing to recover; the device ID alone should not be treated as evidence of an unknown server-bound session.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parse per-record Health Connect checkpoint keys**

Completed Health Connect checkpoints are stored as `@calibrate/health-connect/token/v1/<encoded-origin>/<userId>/<recordType>`, but this pattern accepts only the encoded origin and an optional numeric user ID before the end of the key. Consequently, any user who has completed a Health Connect sync cannot transition to a differently configured service: the valid checkpoint is rejected as an unknown namespace before the token validator below is reached. The parser needs to admit and validate the trailing record-type component.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Addressed in 8e109f51598ce12a2fd0d69503d3432713696f4c. Browser login/register, restoration, logout and revocation retries now share an origin-specific sequence that survives provider remounts. A stale successful response creates durable logout intent and revokes its cookie before replacement credentials run; API requests are blocked during that sequence. Maintained regressions cover late login/register, logout, remounts and failed revocation blocking replacement until recovery. Full mobile suite: 235 suites / 1,332 tests passed.

Addressed in 8e109f51598ce12a2fd0d69503d3432713696f4c. A device ID alone no longer implies an unknown backend identity: the existing token and complete local-state inspection must still prove the installation empty. The regression verifies configured-origin initialization retains the device ID with no active tokens; unknown credential/scoped-data cases remain blocked.

Addressed in 8e109f51598ce12a2fd0d69503d3432713696f4c. Health Connect token keys now validate their origin/account/record-type shape. Regressions preserve checkpoints for all five supported record types and keep unknown record types fail-closed. Stored checkpoint bytes are unchanged.
